authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Cereal production is 1.5x higher, defying 1970s shortage forecasts.
says: In 1985, progression to secondary school (%) was 77.8. By 2017: 91.3 — 1.2 times higher.
In 1972, cereal production was 1083.7 million metric tons. By 2024: 1644.1 million metric tons — 1.5 times higher.
Farmland: China 5.2 million square kilometers, United States 4.2 million, Australia 3.6 million, Brazil 2.4 million, Russia 2.2 million.
authored_explainer.closing: Higher output eased shortage fears, but farmland remains concentrated in a few countries.
authored_explainer.question: Which number changed your view?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Combustible renewables and waste is 3.0x higher than in 1990.
says: In 1990, combustible renewables and waste was 10.2 % of total energy. By 2024: 30.1 % of total energy — 3.0 times higher.
In 1998, access to electricity was 73.2 % of population. By 2024: 91.9 % of population — 1.3 times higher.
In 1972, methane (ch4) emissions from waste was 903.8 Mt CO2e. By 2024: 1,652 Mt CO2e — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Waste can supply energy, but rising methane emissions still affect the climate you live in.
authored_explainer.question: Which tradeoff surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth fell 54% since 1972, reversing runaway-growth fears.
says: In 1972, rural population was 63.1 % of total population. By 2025: 42.2 % of total population — down to 67 percent of that.
In 1972, population in the largest city was 18.2 % of urban population. By 2025: 16.2 % of urban population — barely moved.
In 1972, population growth was 2 annual %. By 2025: 0.91 annual % — down to 46 percent of that.
authored_explainer.closing: Slower growth changes future demand for schools, housing, workers, and care.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift surprised you most?
